question: A shock index (heart rate ÷ systolic blood pressure) of 0.9 or greater in a postpartum woman is a reliable early warning sign of significant haemorrhage requiring urgent intervention, even before the blood pressure falls to a classically 'hypotensive' level.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The shock index (HR/SBP) is a validated early warning sign in obstetric haemorrhage. A value ≥0.9 post-delivery identifies impending haemorrhagic shock even when each parameter alone appears 'normal'. It is integrated into the WHO PPH response algorithm.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. A shock index ≥0.9 in the postpartum period identifies women at risk for severe haemorrhage with greater sensitivity than either HR or BP alone. It is an early warning tool that triggers action before systolic BP drops below 90 mmHg.
